plan: 1 Kings 2:1-9; 2 Samuel 23:1-7; 1 Kings 2:10-12; 1 Chronicles 29:26-30; Psalm 4:1-8; Psalm 5:1-12; Psalm 6:1-10; Psalm 8:1-9; Psalm 9:1-20; Psalm 11:1-7

readings.title: David’s Final Charge to Solomon
readings.subtitle: Walking in the Ways of YeHoVaH
readings.text: [1 Kings 2:1] And the days of Dawiḏ drew near to die, and he commanded <dn>את</dn> Shelomoh his son, saying, [2] “I am going the way of all the earth. And you shall be strong and be a man, [3] and guard <dn>את</dn> the duty to <dn>YeHoVaH your Elohim</dn>, to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways, to guard <dn>His</dn> laws, <dn>His</dn> commands, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, and <dn>His</dn> witnesses, as it is written in the Torah of Mosheh, so that you do wisely in <dn>את</dn> all that you do and wherever you turn, [4] so that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> establishes <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> word which <dn>He</dn> spoke concerning me, saying, <dq>‘If your sons guard their way, to walk before <dn>Me</dn> in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not be a man of yours cut off from the throne of Yisra’ĕl.’</dq> [5] “And you also know <dn>את</dn> what Yo’aḇ son of Tseruyah did to me, and <dn>את</dn> what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Yisra’ĕl, to Aḇnĕr son of Nĕr and Amasa son of Yether, whom he killed. And he shed the blood of battle in peace, and put the blood of battle on his girdle that was on his loins, and on his sandals that were on his feet. [6] “And you shall act according to your wisdom, and do not let his grey hair go down to the grave in peace. [7] “But show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gil‛aḏite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they drew near to me when I fled from Aḇshalom your brother. [8] “And see, you have with you Shim‛i son of Gĕra, a Binyaminite from Baḥurim, who cursed me with a heavy curse in the day when I went to Maḥanayim. But he came down to meet me at the Yardĕn, and I swore to him by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, ‘I do not kill you with the sword.’ [9] “And now, do not leave him unpunished, for you are a wise man and know <dn>את</dn> what you should do to him, and shall bring <dn>את</dn> his grey hair down to the grave with blood.”

readings.title: The Last Words of David
readings.subtitle: The Sweet Psalmist of Yisra’ĕl
readings.text: [2 Samuel 23:1] And these are the last words of Dawiḏ. The saying of Dawiḏ son of Yishai, and the saying of the man raised up on high, the anointed of the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Ya‛aqoḇ, and the sweet psalmist of Yisra’ĕl: [2] “The Spirit of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has spoken by me, and <dn>His</dn> word is on my tongue. [3] “The <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ĕl said, the <dn>Rock of Yisra’ĕl</dn> spoke to me, <dq>‘He who rules over men justly, ruling in the fear of <dn>Elohim</dn>,</dq> [4] <dq>is as the light of the morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, as the tender grass from the earth, from sunshine, from rain.’</dq> [5] “For is not my house so with <dn>El</dn>? For <dn>He</dn> has made an everlasting covenant with me, ordered in all and guarded. For all my deliverance and all desire, would <dn>He</dn> not make it grow? [6] “But the wicked are all as thorns to be thrust away, because they are not taken with hands. [7] “And the man who touches them arms himself with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they are utterly burned with fire in their place.”

readings.title: The Death of David
readings.subtitle: The End of a Forty-Year Reign
readings.text: [1 Kings 2:10] And Dawiḏ slept with his fathers, and was buried in the City of Dawiḏ. [11] And the days that Dawiḏ reigned over Yisra’ĕl were forty years. He reigned seven years in Ḥeḇron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Yerushalayim. [12] And Shelomoh sat on the throne of his father Dawiḏ, and his reign was firmly established. [1 Chronicles 29:26] Thus Dawiḏ son of Yishai reigned over all Yisra’ĕl. [27] And the time that he reigned over Yisra’ĕl was forty years. He reigned seven years in Ḥeḇron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Yerushalayim. [28] And he died in a good old age, satisfied with days, riches and esteem. And Shelomoh his son reigned in his place. [29] And the acts of King Dawiḏ, first and last, see, they are written in the notes of Shemu’ĕl the seer, and in the notes of Nathan the prophet, and in the notes of Gaḏ the seer, [30] with all his reign and his might, and the times that passed over him, and over Yisra’ĕl, and over all the reigns of the lands.

readings.title: An Evening Prayer of Trust
readings.subtitle: Safety in YeHoVaH
readings.text: [Psalm 4:1] Answer me when I call, O <dn>Elohim</dn> of my righteousness! <dn>You</dn> have given me relief in my distress; Show me favour, and hear my prayer. [2] Sons of men, how long is my esteem to be a reproach? How long do you love worthlessness, seek falsehood? Selah. [3] But know that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has separated the kind one for <dn>Himself</dn>; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> hears when I call to <dn>Him</dn>. [4] Tremble, and do not sin. Speak within your heart on your bed, and be still. Selah. [5] Slaughter slaughterings of righteousness, And trust in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [6] Many are saying, “Who does show us good?” <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lift up the light of <dn>Your</dn> face upon us. [7] <dn>You</dn> have put gladness in my heart, More than in the season that their grain and wine increased. [8] I lie down in peace, and sleep altogether; For <dn>You</dn> alone, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, make me dwell in safety.

readings.title: A Morning Prayer for Guidance
readings.subtitle: Confidence in Divine Protection
readings.text: [Psalm 5:1] Give ear to my words, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Consider my meditation. [2] Listen to the voice of my cry, <dn>my King</dn> and <dn>my Elohim</dn>, For to <dn>You</dn> I pray. [3] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, in the morning <dn>You</dn> hear my voice; In the morning I present my case to <dn>You</dn>, and I watch. [4] For <dn>You</dn> are not an <dn>Ěl</dn> pleasant with wickedness, Nor does evil dwell with <dn>You</dn>. [5] The boasters do not stand before <dn>Your</dn> eyes; <dn>You</dn> hate all workers of wickedness. [6] <dn>You</dn> destroy those speaking falsehood; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> abhors a man of blood and deceit. [7] But I, in the longer-lasting of <dn>Your</dn> kindness, I enter <dn>Your</dn> house; I bow myself toward <dn>Your</dn> set-apart Temple in <dn>Your</dn> fear. [8] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, lead me in <dn>Your</dn> righteousness because of my enemies; Make <dn>Your</dn> way straight before my face. [9] For there is no certainty in their mouth; Their inward part is destruction; Their throat is an open grave; They flatter with their tongue. [10] Declare them guilty, O <dn>Elohim</dn>! Let them fall by their own counsels; Banish them in the multitude of their transgressions, For they have rebelled against <dn>You</dn>. [11] But let all who take refuge in <dn>You</dn> rejoice; Let them ever shout for joy, because <dn>You</dn> shelter them; And let those who love <dn>Your</dn> Name exult in <dn>You</dn>. [12] For <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, bless the righteous; With favour <dn>You</dn> surround him as with a shield.

readings.title: A Cry for Mercy in Distress
readings.subtitle: The Soul is Greatly Troubled
readings.text: [Psalm 6:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not reprove me in <dn>Your</dn> displeasure, Nor discipline me in <dn>Your</dn> wrath. [2] Show me favour, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for I am fading away; O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, heal me, for my bones have been troubled. [3] And my soul has been greatly troubled; And <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – how long? [4] Return, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, deliver my soul! Save me because of <dn>Your</dn> kindness. [5] For in death there is no remembrance of <dn>You</dn>; Who gives <dn>You</dn> thanks in the grave? [6] I have grown weary with my groaning; All night I flood my bed; I drench my couch with my tears. [7] My eye has grown dim because of grief; It has grown old because of all my adversaries. [8] Depart from me, all you workers of wickedness; For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard the voice of my weeping. [9] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard my plea; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> receives my prayer. [10] Let all my enemies be ashamed and greatly troubled; Let them turn back, let them be ashamed suddenly.

readings.title: The Majesty of the Creator
readings.subtitle: What is Man that You are Mindful of Him?
readings.text: [Psalm 8:1] O <dn>YeHoVaH our Master</dn>, how excellent is <dn>Your</dn> Name in all the earth, <dn>You</dn> who set <dn>Your</dn> comeliness above the heavens! [2] Out of the mouth of babes and infants <dn>You</dn> have founded strength, Because of <dn>Your</dn> adversaries, To silence the enemy and the avenger. [3] For I look at <dn>Your</dn> heavens, the work of <dn>Your</dn> fingers, The moon and the stars, which <dn>You</dn> have established. [4] What is man that <dn>You</dn> remember him, And the son of man that <dn>You</dn> visit him? [5] For <dn>You</dn> have made him a little lower than <dn>Elohim</dn>, And have crowned him with esteem and comeliness. [6] <dn>You</dn> made him to rule over the works of <dn>Your</dn> hands; <dn>You</dn> have put all under his feet, [7] All sheep and oxen, And also the beasts of the field, [8] The birds of the heavens, and the fish of the sea, Passing through the paths of the seas. [9] O <dn>YeHoVaH our Master</dn>, how excellent is <dn>Your</dn> Name in all the earth!

readings.title: Thanksgiving for Righteous Judgment
readings.subtitle: YeHoVaH Sits on the Throne Forever
readings.text: [Psalm 9:1] I praise <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with all my heart; I declare all <dn>Your</dn> wonders. [2] I rejoice and exult in <dn>You</dn>; I sing praise to <dn>Your</dn> Name, O <dn>Most High</dn>. [3] When my enemies turn back, They stumble and perish from <dn>Your</dn> presence. [4] For <dn>You</dn> have maintained my right and my cause; <dn>You</dn> sat on the throne judging in righteousness. [5] <dn>You</dn> have rebuked the gentiles, <dn>You</dn> have destroyed the wicked; <dn>You</dn> have wiped out their name forever and ever. [6] The enemy is no more – ruins everlasting! And <dn>You</dn> have uprooted the cities; The memory of them has perished. [7] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> abides forever; <dn>He</dn> has prepared <dn>His</dn> throne for judgment. [8] And <dn>He</dn> judges the world in righteousness; <dn>He</dn> judges the peoples in straightness. [9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is a refuge for the crushed, A refuge in times of distress. [10] And those who know <dn>Your</dn> Name trust in <dn>You</dn>, For <dn>You</dn> have not forsaken those who seek <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [11] Sing praises to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who dwells in Tsiyon! Declare <dn>His</dn> deeds among the peoples. [12] For <dn>He</dn> remembers the seekers of blood; <dn>He</dn> has not forgotten the cry of the afflicted. [13] Show me favour, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! See my affliction from those who hate me, <dn>You</dn> who lift me up from the gates of death, [14] So that I declare all <dn>Your</dn> praise In the gates of the daughter of Tsiyon. I rejoice in <dn>Your</dn> deliverance. [15] The gentiles have sunk in the pit they made; In the net which they hid, their own foot is caught. [16] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has made <dn>Himself</dn> known, <dn>He</dn> has done judgment; The wicked is snared in the work of his own hands. Higgayon. Selah. [17] The wicked return to the grave, All the gentiles that forget <dn>Elohim</dn>. [18] For the needy is not always forgotten; The expectancy of the poor does not perish forever. [19] Arise, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, do not let man prevail; Let the gentiles be judged before <dn>Your</dn> face. [20] Put them in fear, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, Let the gentiles know they are but men. Selah.

readings.title: Refuge in the Sovereignty of YeHoVaH
readings.subtitle: His Eyes Behold the Children of Men
readings.text: [Psalm 11:1] In <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> I have taken refuge; How do you say to my soul, “Flee to your mountain like a bird”? [2] For look! The wicked bend the bow, They have set their arrow on the string, To shoot in darkness at the upright in heart. [3] When the foundations are destroyed, What shall the righteous do? [4] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is in <dn>His</dn> set-apart Temple, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>’s throne is in the heavens; <dn>His</dn> eyes see, <dn>His</dn> eyelids examine the sons of men. [5] <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> examines the righteous, But the wicked and the one who loves violence <dn>His</dn> soul hates. [6] Upon the wicked <dn>He</dn> rains snares, fire and sulphur and a burning wind – The portion of their cup. [7] For <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is righteous, <dn>He</dn> has loved righteousness; The upright shall see <dn>His</dn> face.
